event.title: Getting Started with Genealogy – PM
event.description:
Join us for an enlightening 20-minute presentation on “Getting Started with Genealogy,” followed by a 10-minute Q&A session, where your curiosity about tracing your family’s roots can be explored and answered. This engaging session will guide both beginners and those with some experience through the fascinating world of genealogy research.

In this presentation, we will cover the essential steps on how to embark on your genealogy journey, unraveling the secrets of your family’s past. We will share proven methods for genealogy research, including the use of online databases, traditional archival work, and more. Along with these, we’ll provide key tips to enhance your research, making your exploration more efficient and rewarding.

The presentation is offered Tuesday through Friday, at 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM in the Center for Family History Conference room. Don’t miss this opportunity to delve into your family’s history, connect with your ancestors, and discover stories that have shaped who you are today.

Come, uncover your roots, and be a part of this thrilling journey! See you there!

This class is included with your museum admission ticket.

Join us for an enlightening 20-minute presentation on “Getting Started with Genealogy,” followed by a 10-minute Q&A session, where your curiosity about tracing your family’s roots can be explored and answered. This engaging session will guide both beginners and those with some experience through the fascinating world of genealogy research.

In this presentation, we will cover the essential steps on how to embark on your genealogy journey, unraveling the secrets of your family’s past. We will share proven methods for genealogy research, including the use of online databases, traditional archival work, and more. Along with these, we’ll provide key tips to enhance your research, making your exploration more efficient and rewarding.

The presentation is offered Tuesday through Friday, at 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM in the Center for Family History Conference room. Don’t miss this opportunity to delve into your family’s history, connect with your ancestors, and discover stories that have shaped who you are today.

Come, uncover your roots, and be a part of this thrilling journey! See you there!

This class is included with your museum admission ticket.

Join us for an enlightening 20-minute presentation on “Getting Started with Genealogy,” followed by a 10-minute Q&A session, where your curiosity about tracing your family’s roots can be explored and answered. This engaging session will guide both beginners and those with some experience through the fascinating world of genealogy research.

In this presentation, we will cover the essential steps on how to embark on your genealogy journey, unraveling the secrets of your family’s past. We will share proven methods for genealogy research, including the use of online databases, traditional archival work, and more. Along with these, we’ll provide key tips to enhance your research, making your exploration more efficient and rewarding.

The presentation is offered Tuesday through Friday, at 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM in the Center for Family History Conference room. Don’t miss this opportunity to delve into your family’s history, connect with your ancestors, and discover stories that have shaped who you are today.

Come, uncover your roots, and be a part of this thrilling journey! See you there!

This class is included with your museum admission ticket.

Join us for an enlightening 20-minute presentation on “Getting Started with Genealogy,” followed by a 10-minute Q&A session, where your curiosity about tracing your family’s roots can be explored and answered. This engaging session will guide both beginners and those with some experience through the fascinating world of genealogy research.

In this presentation, we will cover the essential steps on how to embark on your genealogy journey, unraveling the secrets of your family’s past. We will share proven methods for genealogy research, including the use of online databases, traditional archival work, and more. Along with these, we’ll provide key tips to enhance your research, making your exploration more efficient and rewarding.

The presentation is offered Tuesday through Friday, at 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM in the Center for Family History Conference room. Don’t miss this opportunity to delve into your family’s history, connect with your ancestors, and discover stories that have shaped who you are today.

Come, uncover your roots, and be a part of this thrilling journey! See you there!

This class is included with your museum admission ticket.

event.title: StartupBREW Fargo 09/30/26
event.description:
StartupBREW Fargo is a weekly networking event in Fargo held at the Prairie Den on Wednesday mornings from 8:00 AM – 9:30 AM.

This event is built on the notion that entrepreneurs do better when they have access to each other and the greater community that supports them. Entrepreneurship is energized over brews – coffee, tea, beer or others. Connection over coffee has been at the center of energizing our community, which is where the name StartupBREW came from.

At the core, this event will place an emphasis on connection in the program by limiting individual speaking time and increasing conversation. This is practiced through Coffee Club, a time to connect before the event, as well as a 20-minute Q+A session with the audience towards the end of the program.

Minnesota State University Moorhead Takeover Day will bring a special StartupBREW experience to campus, creating another opportunity for the Fargo-Moorhead community to connect, learn and engage with new ideas.

FORE! Mental Health Charity Golf Event
event.description:
PCL Construction will host the inaugural North Dakota edition of its FORE! Mental Health Charity Golf Event, bringing together industry leaders, trade partners, clients and community supporters to raise awareness and funds for mental health and suicide prevention initiatives.

The event comes at a pivotal time for the construction industry and serves as part of the broader effort to raise awareness during Construction Suicide Prevention Week (September 14-18), a global initiative focused on addressing the industry’s elevated suicide risk and expanding access to mental health resources and support. By bringing together stakeholders from across North Dakota’s construction community, PCL continues to demonstrate its commitment to advancing conversations around mental wellbeing, connecting people with available resources and fostering supportive workplace cultures across the industry.

Proceeds from the event will support the 4-6-3 Foundation, an organization dedicated to suicide prevention and mental wellness in our community. Through its work, the foundation advances mental health awareness, advocacy, and access to resources for individuals and families affected by mental health challenges.

PCL has supported the foundation’s mission as a presenting sponsor of the annual Liam G. Medd Baseball Tournament, furthering efforts to raise awareness and support mental wellness throughout the community.

event.title: What’s Your Roadmap? Helpful Tips For Living Your Best Life
event.description:
Join HIA Health for a community education event on Wednesday, September 30 at HIA Health!

Life doesn’t always follow the path we expected. Whether you’re managing a chronic condition, caring for a loved one, planning, or simply wanting to make informed healthcare decisions, HIA Health invites community members to attend “What’s Your Roadmap? Helpful Tips For Living Your Best Life.”

HIA Hospice Medical Director Dr. Mark Rostad, HIA Primary Care at Home Medical Director Dr. Lara Lunde, HIA Health Primary Care Clinic Medical Director Dr. Kinsey Nelson, and HIA Hospice Ancillary Services Manager Katie Ambuehl will lead the conversation to give attendees practical tools to help you navigate your journey with confidence.

Attendees will leave with actionable tips, local resources, and a personal planning guide designed to help organize important information and document what matters most.

These community education events are free and open to the public.

D&D One-Shot Wednesdays are exactly what they sound like: self-contained adventures that begin and end in one night. Show up, grab a seat, and play.

MARCELLA ARGUELLO
Marcella is an actor, writer and stand up comedian of twenty years. She will discuss any and every topic that tickles her but you can often hear her joke about her Latinx identity, her takes on race & gender, and wild stories & situations she’s gotten herself in and out of. Marcella’s debut half hour comedy special Bitch, Grow Up. was released in 2023 on HBO MAX. It’s a half hour that fully represents the comedians ability to handle all forms of comedy – from one liners to stories to crowd work – the many years of working the road shines through. Of the special, Latin Media writes that Marcella “manages to ruffle feathers while delivering a routine that feels absolutely joyous.” Decider.com writes, “she has earned this moment.”
In 2025, Marcella can be seen as the new guidance counselor, Ms. Alomar, on Abbott Elementary on ABC. She was crowned the champion of After Midnight on CBS, where she also made a great first impression in 2024, according to Vulture. She can also be seen on the second season of Poker Face on Peacock. She relocated to Chicago where she runs her show, Comedy Is Dead! at The Den Theatre on the first Thursday of the month. The show is a result of her podcast of the same name, which tackles her experience with the industry and why she feels stand up is currently in a strange place. The second season welcomes a new cohost, Chloe Mikala and is currently streaming on YouTube. She is also currently working on her first solo show, coming to a black box theatre near you in 2026.
She is most proud of her formerly monthly show, Women Crush Wednesdays, which always had a fresh and diverse line up, including national headliners as well as the brightest up and comers. Marcella mercilessly hosted the best curated show in all of Los Angeles while providing numerous opportunities to many comedians because of it; occasionally she takes the show on the road: Women Crush Wednesdays has popped up in Toronto, Canada, Chicago and has been featured at SF Sketchfest, as well as The Ford in Los Angeles. Her debut album, The Woke Bully – which debuted at #3 on the Billboard Comedy Charts and was named One Of The Best Comedy Albums of 2019 by NPR program Bullseye – is a combination of Marcella’s unique perspective & honesty and captures what it’s like to experience her live. Her follow up album, Mercury in Reggaeton, is a collection of rejected material from her debut special and is a perfect depiction of her ability to go with the flow of a live show. Marcella also recorded Motivational Monday Meditations with Marcella Marguello, a comedic meditation album that is beloved by anyone who listens.
In 2023, she was a featured player on Fuse TV’s We Need To Talk About America, where first generation comedians dissected American-centric topics and viral videos. Marcella was also the host of The Cache on Tubi in 2021, a hilarious clip show that infuses Marcella’s unique perspective on viral videos. In 2020, COVID-19 halted the entertainment industry but Marcella managed to guest star in Sarah Cooper’s Netflix Special Everything’s Fine, was seen as a panelist on David Spade’s Lights Out on Comedy Central, killed her over-the-top dance numbers on The Funny Dance Show on E! and had a covid compliant interview on FuseTV’s Like, Share, Dímelo. Her stand up can be seen on the second season of 2 Dope Queens on HBO as well as Night Train with Wyatt Cenac on STARZ; previously she has made a guest appearance on Comedy Central’s Corporate and on episodes of FuseTV’s Trivial Takedown. Recently MSN.com listed Marcella as number 10 in their list of “Top female comedians working in film and television today.” In the Fall of 2017, Vulture.com presented their list of “Comedians You Should and Will Know” and Marcella was the top industry pick which gaind her a feature in the November issue of New York Magazine. Marcella was deemed an “LA Comedian to Watch in 2017” by Time Out Magazine while maintaining her reign as a fan favorite and six-time winner on Comedy Central’s @midnight. She wrote for the renewed Netflix series “Bill Nye Saves The World” and was a writer on the first season of the James Corden-produced show, Drop The Mic on TBS. Additionally, Marcella won her appearance on TruTv’s Comedy Knock Out, was featured on Viceland’s Flophouse, and in 2015 on NBC’s Last Call with Carson Daly; her stand up has been highlighted on rapper Tyler, The Creator’s mobile app and on Fox’s The Real.
Her controversial takes on Twitter (@marcellacomedy) have featured the comedian on CNN, Glamor Magazine, Fox, TIME.com, HuffingtonPost.com and various other entertainment websites. She currently hates social media but you can still find her actively running her mouth on various sites such as Instagram, Threads and Blue Sky.
Marcella is a regular opener for Felipe Esparza, Hasan Minhaj, Ralph Barbosa, Nicole Byer, Melissa Villaseñor and Nico Santos. She has previously opened for Marcello Hernandez, Ramy Youseff, Michelle Buteau, Hannibal Buress, David Alan Grier, Cheech Marin, Norm MacDonald, J.B. Smoove, Aida Rodriguez, Phoebe Robinson, Al Madrigal, Ron Funches, Godfrey, Pablo Francisco, Joey Coco Diaz, Melanie Comarcho and many more. She has also had the privilege of sharing the stage with Bill Burr, Mark Curry, Janeane Garofalo, Fred Armisen, Quinta Brunson, Bowen Yang, Jerry Seinfeld, Paul Mooney and Robin Williams.
Her love of music has also allowed her to rock a stage with many artists she admires such as Black Thought, Jean Grae, Freddie Gibbs, MURS, Del The Funky Homosapien, Immortal Technique, Dead Prez, Too $hort and E40. As well as having worked with Method Man, Usher, Quelle Chris, Fat Tony, and Tyler, The Creator.
Additionally, she has proudly graced the television stage with Sheryl Lee Ralph, Marisa Tomei, Natasha Lyonne, Lisa Ann Walter, Affion Crocket, Emily Althaus, Thomas Lennon, Gillian Jacobs and Weird Al Yankovic, just to name a few.

She has worked at The Improv Comedy Clubs all over the country and is a regular at The Punch Line Comedy Clubs in Northern California. She has headlined the Latina Comedy Festival, the Detroit Women of Comedy Festival and the B4UDie Festival in Alaska. She has also performed at The New York Comedy Festival, Bridgetown Comedy Festival, Chris Hardwick’s ID10T Festival, Riot LA Comedy Festival, Lucille Ball Comedy Fest, overseas for American troops and comedian Sean Keane referred to her as the “finest export from Modesto since George Lucas.”

event.description:
Fish Tank Promotions is proud to present Missouri Executive Order 44 with MΩTHER, Antler, and JURON at The Aquarium in Fargo on Friday, October 2.

8 PM doors • 8:30 PM music • 21+ event

Based in Kansas City, Missouri Executive Order 44 takes its name from a dark chapter of its state’s history. In 1838, amidst tensions between Missouri residents and a burgeoning new Mormon population, Governor Lilburn Boggs issued an order stating, “The Mormons must be treated as enemies, and must be exterminated or driven from the state if necessary for the public peace.”

Clad in the bike helmets and white shirts that commonly signify LDS evangelists, the four members of MEO44 – vocalist Jarom Johnson, guitarist Elos Olsen, bassist Esau Fullmer, and drummer Malachi Hatch – use that specific historical moment as their rallying cry as they blast out blistering hardcore anthems in opposition to all forms of persecution.

Olsen states: “The struggle against fascist violent oppression of ‘undesirables’ is universal. We use a very fucked-up moment of hyper-localized American history to relay that message for the fight against oppression. It’s a purely anti-authoritarian band. Don’t let anyone tell you who to love or who to worship.”

Johnson concurs: “Missouri Executive Order 44 is a reminder that we, as decent human beings, need to stand together in communities and collectives to overthrow tyrannical authority and prevent the impending destruction of our autonomy by the bigoted forces of the state, police, and fascists. The story of our Mormon ascendants is cautionary but also too familiar to the experiences of our brothers and sisters. The state can and will oppress those it deems ‘other’ or ‘less than,’ and our message is one of retribution, anti-colonialism, anti-state, and pro-humanity.”

MΩTHER is shouty post-hardcore/screamo out of Fargo.

Antler is black metal crust featuring members of MAUL and Disappear Forever.

JURON brings the heavy.

event.title: Whiskey Class – Asian Whiskey
event.description:
Taste examples of whiskey from across Asia with Evan Christie

Distillation was invented at least two separate times on the vast Asian continent, which gave rise to many popular local spirits. Yet there is no denying that Whiskey, as it grew out of Northern Europe, has captured the hearts and the imaginations of certain distillers consumers across Asia. From Japan, whose whiskey industry was the result of cultural exchange in the early 1900s, to India, where post-colonial yearning spurred a native grown tradition, to Taiwan, where the powers of global capitalism have given rise to new and popular producers.

In this class, Evan Christie will lead an exploration of the many whiskies of Asia. Expect mainly malt whiskies with influences from Scotland and beyond. Learn how historic and economic forces have shaped the state of whiskey in Asia and how the continent is posed for more growth and innovation. Taste the wonderful world of Asian whiskey with us today!

There is something special about a room full of gamers.

On any given Sunday at Paradox Comics-N-Cards, you might find adventurers exploring a forgotten dungeon, heroes saving a kingdom, rival starships battling across a tabletop, commanders shuffling up for one more game, or friends gathered around a board game they have been meaning to try for months. Sunday Game Day is our weekly celebration of tabletop gaming in all its forms.

The tables are open, the community is welcoming, and the possibilities are nearly endless. Bring your favorite board game, roleplaying game, miniature game, card game, or campaign group and settle in for an afternoon of gaming. Whether you arrive with a full party or come looking for fellow players, Sunday is one of the best times to connect with the local gaming community.

Roleplaying games are especially at home on Sundays. Gather your adventuring party, continue an ongoing campaign, introduce new players to the hobby, or launch something completely new. From Dungeons & Dragons to Pathfinder, Call of Cthulhu, Star Wars, and countless other RPGs, our tables are available for stories waiting to be told.

Board gamers are equally welcome. Strategy games, family games, co-op adventures, deckbuilders, party games, and everything in between all have a place here. Our game library is available to browse, and you’re always welcome to bring games from home as well.

While open gaming is the heart of Sunday Game Day, we occasionally schedule organized events, demos, leagues, and special gaming activities throughout the year. If you enjoy tabletop gaming, we encourage you to bookmark the Paradox Comics-N-Cards event calendar and check back often. You never know when your next favorite game, campaign, or event might appear.

There is no entry fee for Sunday Game Day. Just bring your games, your imagination, and your sense of adventure.

event.description:
StartupBREW Fargo is a weekly networking event in Fargo held at the Prairie Den on Wednesday mornings from 8:00 AM – 9:30 AM.

This event is built on the notion that entrepreneurs do better when they have access to each other and the greater community that supports them. Entrepreneurship is energized over brews – coffee, tea, beer or others. Connection over coffee has been at the center of energizing our community, which is where the name StartupBREW came from.

At the core, this event will place an emphasis on connection in the program by limiting individual speaking time and increasing conversation. This is practiced through Coffee Club, a time to connect before the event, as well as a 20-minute Q+A session with the audience towards the end of the program.

event.description:
There is something special about sitting down at a table with a good game, a few friends, and no rush to be anywhere else.

Every Thursday night, Paradox Comics-N-Cards opens the tables for a completely free evening of casual board gaming. Whether you are bringing your longtime favorite game, trying something brand new, or simply looking for a place to meet other people who enjoy boardgames, Thursday night is the perfect time to hang out at 814 Main Avenue. It’s relaxed, welcoming, and easy to jump into.

Bring your own games, teach something you love, learn something new, or just wander from table to table seeing what everyone is playing. Some groups will be deep into strategy games. Others might be laughing through party games, battling through co-op adventures, or introducing new players to modern board gaming for the very first time. No tournament pressure. No entry fee. Just a great night of gaming with good people.

You do not need a full group to attend. One of the best parts of board game night is meeting new players and discovering games you may never have tried otherwise. If you are new to tabletop gaming, this is also a great way to get started. Our community is filled with people who love sharing the hobby.

Our game library will be available to browse throughout the evening, and you are always welcome to bring games from home as well. Feel free to arrive early, stay late, grab snacks, settle in, and make a night of it.

If you have been looking for a regular place to unplug for a few hours, roll some dice, play some cards, and spend time with other gamers, Thursday nights at Paradox are for you.

event.title: LunaTique’s Booze, Brothels, & Boos Downtown Fargo ND Walking History Tour
event.description:
A two-hour historical walking tour of downtown Fargo, ND, covering the Wild West & more!

LunaTique Boutique presents the Booze, Brothels, & Boos Tour !

That’s “booze,” as in liquor, “brothels,” as in, well, we think you know, and “boos,” as in hauntings & ghost stories. Hence, this tour is also known as the Nice Jugs Tour. Our stories begin nearly 170 years ago, in the late 1850s, when the Dakota Territory didn’t even exist yet.

Get ready to hear about an eccentric assortment of folks who not only embodied the spirit of the American frontier, but some of whom may have left some spirits behind too… Hear about those in the saloon & brothel industries, what the early citizenry really thought of them, and true stories of ghostly activities.

This in-person event is perfect for thrill-seekers and history buffs alike. This two-hour historical walking tour in downtown Fargo will be led by the proprietress herself, The Purple-Haired Crone, Deanna Dahlsad.

Get ready for a scandalous & spooky adventure through the streets & history of downtown Fargo! This is an adult tour for ages 16 and up. This tour will present adult deeds & not-so-nice things from our past; please use your discretion in signing up for this tour. Don’t miss out on this unforgettable journey into sin & the supernatural world of the early years of downtown Fargo. Please arrive 20 minutes before the tour start time.

NOTE: Purchase of a ticket is an agreement for yourself (& any minor children in your care) that:

  • You take this tour voluntarily.
  • You understand this is a walking tour, that you are in good health and will dress accordingly, & that there are risks to walking tours.
  • You accept personal responsibility for anything that happens to you during a tour, & release LunaTique Boutique & any affiliates from any claims or liability for damages.
  • Prepare to be startled by things that go bump (& grind!) in the night!!

event.description:
Come join us for a night filled with soulful tunes at TAK Music Venue! We’re celebrating the legendary Carole King with our annual tribute event, Raspberry Jam. Get ready to sing along to her timeless classics and enjoy a night of music and memories. This in-person event is a must-attend for any Carole King fan, for those who have loved her music for decades or those who are just getting familiar with this multi-Grammy award winning American songwriter and performer.

SPECIAL FOR THE 2026 PROGRAM — The Raspberry Jam Band is honoring the 55th anniversary of both albums that were released in 1971: the iconic & influential “Tapestry” as well as King’s third record, “Music”, which was released a mere ten months after “Tapestry”. To pay homage to the rich catalogue of influential chart-topping hits contained within the “Tapestry” songlist, the tunes from that album will be performed exclusively during the second set. Don’t miss out on this unforgettable evening!

To start off the event, culinary delights from Deb’s Corner Foods are available for purchase! Deb returns as the official vendor for the evening, serving delicious meals and snacks to please the palates of carnivorous and vegetarian/vegan attendees alike. Deb’s concessions will be available as soon as the doors open and will continue through the end of intermission or until supplies run out. The venue will also have a variety of cold beverages available for purchase, including plenty of options for adult libations at the full-service bar (with proof of ID).

All ages are welcome at this show! Children under 7 attend for FREE!

All ticketholders will have access to a round or a hightop table for enjoying the social hour and performance. Seats are not assigned and will be available on a first-come-first-served basis.

  • General Admission: $19.71
  • ADA Admission: $19.71
  • VIP Admission: $25 – Special VIP section including the tables closest to the front; seats are unassigned

STUDENTS: Show your valid school ID to receive $10 admission at the door!!! This includes Elementary, Junior/Senior High, and all College/University student identification cards.

Any remaining general admission tickets will be sold for $25 at the door (cash price; credit card fees apply to all at-the-door ticket sales)

The Raspberry Jam Crew are pleased to partner with Schmitt Music for the third year in a row, and the star of the show will once again be the acoustic baby grand piano for this performance. Many thanks to our new partner Golden Touch Moving, who has faithfully provided excellent piano moving services for all of the Raspberry Jam events held at TAK.

To keep connected, please visit: www.facebook.com/RaspberryJamTributeBand

The current roster of the Raspberry Jam Band includes: Kari Marie del Rio (piano, vocals), Cayden Ganser (guitar), Matthew Tinjum (drums), Doug Neill (bass), and “Dakota Kate” Henne (harmonica, mandolin, violin). Featured vocalists include Andi Thoreson and Sarah Morrau. Several special guests will be joining the band throughout the evening, providing a full sound with a horns section and second keyboardist.

October 9, 2026, will mark the eighth presentation of the Raspberry Jam tribute show and the third year at TAK Music Venue, having been previously held at the former HoDo Lounge and Concordia College.

event.title: Sunday Game Day
event.description:
There is something special about a room full of gamers.

On any given Sunday at Paradox Comics-N-Cards, you might find adventurers exploring a forgotten dungeon, heroes saving a kingdom, rival starships battling across a tabletop, commanders shuffling up for one more game, or friends gathered around a board game they have been meaning to try for months. Sunday Game Day is our weekly celebration of tabletop gaming in all its forms.

The tables are open, the community is welcoming, and the possibilities are nearly endless. Bring your favorite board game, roleplaying game, miniature game, card game, or campaign group and settle in for an afternoon of gaming. Whether you arrive with a full party or come looking for fellow players, Sunday is one of the best times to connect with the local gaming community.

Roleplaying games are especially at home on Sundays. Gather your adventuring party, continue an ongoing campaign, introduce new players to the hobby, or launch something completely new. From Dungeons & Dragons to Pathfinder, Call of Cthulhu, Star Wars, and countless other RPGs, our tables are available for stories waiting to be told.

Board gamers are equally welcome. Strategy games, family games, co-op adventures, deckbuilders, party games, and everything in between all have a place here. Our game library is available to browse, and you’re always welcome to bring games from home as well.

While open gaming is the heart of Sunday Game Day, we occasionally schedule organized events, demos, leagues, and special gaming activities throughout the year. If you enjoy tabletop gaming, we encourage you to bookmark the Paradox Comics-N-Cards event calendar and check back often. You never know when your next favorite game, campaign, or event might appear.

There is no entry fee for Sunday Game Day. Just bring your games, your imagination, and your sense of adventure.

event.title: Spirits Class – Autumnal Gin
event.description:
Taste gin whose flavor profiles are a great fit for fall with Evan Christie

The bright, botanical flavors of gin are so intensely linked with summer that the season and the spirit can seem made for each other, yet in a world where distillers have expanded the definitions of gin so broadly, many include botanicals that foster flavor profiles suited to any season. Darker, richer gins make this delightful spirit fit not just for the heat of summer but for the cool breeze of autumn.

In this class Evan Christie will lead you on an exploration of gins that fit the seasonal sensibilities of autumn. Expect notes of spice, fall fruits, and other flavors that are generally associated with this time of year. You will learn what makes these gins special and discuss how they may work well in seasonal cocktails. Join us for an eye-opening experience in seasonal drinking.

event.title: Cocktail Class – The Mai Tai
event.description:
Taste and learn about variations of the illustrious Mai Tai with Evan Christie

The Mai-Tai is one of the most iconic tiki drinks in history and also one of the most often botched. Trader Vic’s classic mixture of rum, orgeat, orange liqueur, and lime juice is a boozy, rich, and balanced tipple, yet copy cats abound, many of which are replete with a host of juices and syrups that were never called for. As the classic recipe has again taken hold, there have been a spate of new variations that stay faithful to the original formula.

In this class, Evan Christie will explore the history of the Mai Tai and the wonderful variations that now exist of this classic drink. Expect to be transported away by the subtle potions of tiki escapism while learning about how the Mai Tai became of the best known drinks of the 20th century, even as the original version became of the least known. You will taste new and wonderful variations on the classic Mai Tai template, exploring what is at the core of the iconic beverage.

event.title: Sunday Game Day
event.description:
There is something special about a room full of gamers.

On any given Sunday at Paradox Comics-N-Cards, you might find adventurers exploring a forgotten dungeon, heroes saving a kingdom, rival starships battling across a tabletop, commanders shuffling up for one more game, or friends gathered around a board game they have been meaning to try for months. Sunday Game Day is our weekly celebration of tabletop gaming in all its forms.

The tables are open, the community is welcoming, and the possibilities are nearly endless. Bring your favorite board game, roleplaying game, miniature game, card game, or campaign group and settle in for an afternoon of gaming. Whether you arrive with a full party or come looking for fellow players, Sunday is one of the best times to connect with the local gaming community.

Roleplaying games are especially at home on Sundays. Gather your adventuring party, continue an ongoing campaign, introduce new players to the hobby, or launch something completely new. From Dungeons & Dragons to Pathfinder, Call of Cthulhu, Star Wars, and countless other RPGs, our tables are available for stories waiting to be told.

Board gamers are equally welcome. Strategy games, family games, co-op adventures, deckbuilders, party games, and everything in between all have a place here. Our game library is available to browse, and you’re always welcome to bring games from home as well.

While open gaming is the heart of Sunday Game Day, we occasionally schedule organized events, demos, leagues, and special gaming activities throughout the year. If you enjoy tabletop gaming, we encourage you to bookmark the Paradox Comics-N-Cards event calendar and check back often. You never know when your next favorite game, campaign, or event might appear.

There is no entry fee for Sunday Game Day. Just bring your games, your imagination, and your sense of adventure.

Beyond the Brief w/ Matt Dawson
event.description:
Beyond the Brief is about creating just because you can, want to, or need to and discovering where it takes you.

“Beyond the Brief” with Matt Dawson

Join us for our 2nd speaker event of our 2026-27 season, “Beyond the Brief” with Matt Dawson, Creative Director.

Presentation Overview:
Most creative work starts with a brief. But sometimes you make something just because you can, because you want to, or because you can’t stop thinking about it.

Beyond the Brief is about making those things. The things nobody asked for. The things that reconnect you with why you started creating in the first place. And the things that, every now and then, lead to surprising benefits and unexpected opportunities.

Speaker Bio:
Matt Dawson is an Austin-based Creative Director and designer known for bold, polished work across branding, illustration, and typography. He’s collaborated with clients like Jeep, Major League Baseball, Pearl Jam, Phish, Toyota, and Disney, bringing a sharp eye and strong visual voice to every project. Over the past 20 years, he’s worked with global brands, scrappy startups, and yes, maybe even one of your favorite bands. The quality and respect of his work has led to features in books, magazines, and blogs, as well as invitations to speak on stages across the country.

He’s also the founder of Crop, a grassroots creative conference in Austin with a punk rock spirit and a focus on building genuine creative community. The event features keynote talks, hands-on workshops, vendors, live music, parties, creative activations, and more. Since launching in 2016, Crop has brought together over 3,000 creatives from 35 states and 6 countries. It’s become known for its “come as you are” vibe where first-timers and longtime attendees alike immediately feel part of the community.

Entrepreneurship is energized over brews – coffee, tea, beer or others. Connection over coffee has been at the center of energizing our community, which is where the name StartupBREW came from.

At the core, this event will place an emphasis on connection in the program by limiting individual speaking time and increasing conversation. This is practiced through Coffee Club, a time to connect before the event, as well as a 20-minute Q+A session with the audience towards the end of the program.

Minnesota State Community and Technical College Moorhead Takeover Day will bring a special lineup and fresh perspectives to the StartupBREW stage, giving the community another opportunity to connect, learn and engage with new ideas.

event.description:
There is something special about sitting down at a table with a good game, a few friends, and no rush to be anywhere else.

Every Thursday night, Paradox Comics-N-Cards opens the tables for a completely free evening of casual board gaming. Whether you are bringing your longtime favorite game, trying something brand new, or simply looking for a place to meet other people who enjoy boardgames, Thursday night is the perfect time to hang out at 814 Main Avenue. It’s relaxed, welcoming, and easy to jump into.

Bring your own games, teach something you love, learn something new, or just wander from table to table seeing what everyone is playing. Some groups will be deep into strategy games. Others might be laughing through party games, battling through co-op adventures, or introducing new players to modern board gaming for the very first time. No tournament pressure. No entry fee. Just a great night of gaming with good people.

You do not need a full group to attend. One of the best parts of board game night is meeting new players and discovering games you may never have tried otherwise. If you are new to tabletop gaming, this is also a great way to get started. Our community is filled with people who love sharing the hobby.

Our game library will be available to browse throughout the evening, and you are always welcome to bring games from home as well. Feel free to arrive early, stay late, grab snacks, settle in, and make a night of it.

If you have been looking for a regular place to unplug for a few hours, roll some dice, play some cards, and spend time with other gamers, Thursday nights at Paradox are for you.

event.title: Wine Class – Skin Contact: Reds and Whites
event.description:
Join sommelier Josh Voytek on an exploration of how skin contact affects wines, through the lense of orange wines and chillable reds

Join Certified Sommelier Josh Voytek of Rootstock Wine Company for an exploration of what effect adjusting the usual amount of grape skin contact during the fermentation process has on grapes. Typically, most folks have a general concept of the color that most red and white wines in the market look like. However, there is a historic category of white wines called orange or amber wines due to the fact that they take on a deeper color due to increased skin contact. This results in white wines that are darker in color and contain tannins and overall drink more like red wines. On the other side, besides roses, there are red wines that are intentionally made with limited skin contact and often little to no oak, designed to be fresh, fruity and chillable. In other words, to be drank more like white wines. In this wine class, we will try examples of “orange” whites and light “chillable” reds that expand the perception of what “traditional” wine should be. In both cases, these wines are great for the fall and pairing with fall foods, so come to learn about these wines but also to perhaps find a new seasonal favorite.

event.title: Sunday Game Day
event.description:
There is something special about a room full of gamers.

On any given Sunday at Paradox Comics-N-Cards, you might find adventurers exploring a forgotten dungeon, heroes saving a kingdom, rival starships battling across a tabletop, commanders shuffling up for one more game, or friends gathered around a board game they have been meaning to try for months. Sunday Game Day is our weekly celebration of tabletop gaming in all its forms.

The tables are open, the community is welcoming, and the possibilities are nearly endless. Bring your favorite board game, roleplaying game, miniature game, card game, or campaign group and settle in for an afternoon of gaming. Whether you arrive with a full party or come looking for fellow players, Sunday is one of the best times to connect with the local gaming community.

Roleplaying games are especially at home on Sundays. Gather your adventuring party, continue an ongoing campaign, introduce new players to the hobby, or launch something completely new. From Dungeons & Dragons to Pathfinder, Call of Cthulhu, Star Wars, and countless other RPGs, our tables are available for stories waiting to be told.

Board gamers are equally welcome. Strategy games, family games, co-op adventures, deckbuilders, party games, and everything in between all have a place here. Our game library is available to browse, and you’re always welcome to bring games from home as well.

While open gaming is the heart of Sunday Game Day, we occasionally schedule organized events, demos, leagues, and special gaming activities throughout the year. If you enjoy tabletop gaming, we encourage you to bookmark the Paradox Comics-N-Cards event calendar and check back often. You never know when your next favorite game, campaign, or event might appear.

There is no entry fee for Sunday Game Day. Just bring your games, your imagination, and your sense of adventure.
event.excerpt: Sunday Game Day is our weekly celebration of tabletop gaming in all its forms.

Alt RPG Day goes monthly at Paradox Comics-N-Cards.

Dungeons & Dragons may be the biggest name in role-playing games, but it’s far from the only one—and some of the most exciting RPGs out there live just outside the D&D bubble. That’s what this day is for.

Each month we’ll be running non-D&D role-playing games. The exact systems will change month to month depending on what our DMs are excited to run—and that’s part of the fun. You don’t need to know the game ahead of time. You just need to show up ready to play.

This is a great day to:

  • Try a new RPG without committing to a campaign
  • Learn a system you’ve been curious about
  • Sit down with a table of players who want to explore something different

WE’RE ALSO LOOKING FOR DMs

If you’re a DM who loves non-D&D systems and wants an excuse to put something cool on the table, we want you.

  • Run what you’re excited about
  • One-shots or short arcs work best

event.title: StartupBREW Fargo 10/28/26
event.description:
StartupBREW Fargo is a weekly networking event in Fargo held at the Prairie Den on Wednesday mornings from 8:00 AM – 9:30 AM.

This event is built on the notion that entrepreneurs do better when they have access to each other and the greater community that supports them. Entrepreneurship is energized over brews – coffee, tea, beer or others. Connection over coffee has been at the center of energizing our community, which is where the name StartupBREW came from.

At the core, this event will place an emphasis on connection in the program by limiting individual speaking time and increasing conversation. This is practiced through Coffee Club, a time to connect before the event, as well as a 20-minute Q+A session with the audience towards the end of the program.

Upcoming speakers include Dr. Joseph Marion of Vascular Care, sharing his experience building and growing a healthcare business, and Spencer Marchand, founder and chairman of Dakota Linen Co., a longtime local company providing linen and textile services to businesses. Together, they bring diverse perspectives on entrepreneurship, leadership, and building businesses in the Fargo-Moorhead community.

event.description:

This evening features Ron Offutt, founder and Chairman Emeritus of R.D. Offutt Company and RDO Equipment Co. What began with a family farming operation in the Red River Valley grew into one of North America’s largest agricultural equipment organizations, built on a commitment to serving growers, investing in people, and thinking for the long term.

Join us as Ron reflects on the defining moments of his career, the challenges that shaped his leadership, and the lessons learned from building businesses that have left a lasting mark on agriculture across America.

event.description:
There is something special about sitting down at a table with a good game, a few friends, and no rush to be anywhere else.

Every Thursday night, Paradox Comics-N-Cards opens the tables for a completely free evening of casual board gaming. Whether you are bringing your longtime favorite game, trying something brand new, or simply looking for a place to meet other people who enjoy boardgames, Thursday night is the perfect time to hang out at 814 Main Avenue. It’s relaxed, welcoming, and easy to jump into.

Bring your own games, teach something you love, learn something new, or just wander from table to table seeing what everyone is playing. Some groups will be deep into strategy games. Others might be laughing through party games, battling through co-op adventures, or introducing new players to modern board gaming for the very first time. No tournament pressure. No entry fee. Just a great night of gaming with good people.

You do not need a full group to attend. One of the best parts of board game night is meeting new players and discovering games you may never have tried otherwise. If you are new to tabletop gaming, this is also a great way to get started. Our community is filled with people who love sharing the hobby.

Our game library will be available to browse throughout the evening, and you are always welcome to bring games from home as well. Feel free to arrive early, stay late, grab snacks, settle in, and make a night of it.

If you have been looking for a regular place to unplug for a few hours, roll some dice, play some cards, and spend time with other gamers, Thursday nights at Paradox are for you.

event.title: Sunday Game Day
event.description:
There is something special about a room full of gamers.

On any given Sunday at Paradox Comics-N-Cards, you might find adventurers exploring a forgotten dungeon, heroes saving a kingdom, rival starships battling across a tabletop, commanders shuffling up for one more game, or friends gathered around a board game they have been meaning to try for months. Sunday Game Day is our weekly celebration of tabletop gaming in all its forms.

The tables are open, the community is welcoming, and the possibilities are nearly endless. Bring your favorite board game, roleplaying game, miniature game, card game, or campaign group and settle in for an afternoon of gaming. Whether you arrive with a full party or come looking for fellow players, Sunday is one of the best times to connect with the local gaming community.

Roleplaying games are especially at home on Sundays. Gather your adventuring party, continue an ongoing campaign, introduce new players to the hobby, or launch something completely new. From Dungeons & Dragons to Pathfinder, Call of Cthulhu, Star Wars, and countless other RPGs, our tables are available for stories waiting to be told.

Board gamers are equally welcome. Strategy games, family games, co-op adventures, deckbuilders, party games, and everything in between all have a place here. Our game library is available to browse, and you’re always welcome to bring games from home as well.

While open gaming is the heart of Sunday Game Day, we occasionally schedule organized events, demos, leagues, and special gaming activities throughout the year. If you enjoy tabletop gaming, we encourage you to bookmark the Paradox Comics-N-Cards event calendar and check back often. You never know when your next favorite game, campaign, or event might appear.

There is no entry fee for Sunday Game Day. Just bring your games, your imagination, and your sense of adventure.
